observations: body L1-L2: «Maslamah al–Maǵrīṭī» is letter-spaced; «ar–Raqqah», «241,v.–244,r.» and «al–Maǵrīṭī» have long dashes (5.5 pt each).
body L5-L6: the dashes after «a)» and «I.» measure 10.0 and 9.6 pt; «19-33» has a hyphen (3.4 pt).

body L7-L11: «Ptolemaeus», «al–Battānī» and «aṣ–Ṣūfī» are letter-spaced, the last two with long dashes (5.5 and 5.2 pt); the dash after «Chr.» (L8) measures 8.3 pt. The year 885 of Nabonassar began on 20 July 137 and the year 845 on 30 July 97 (Julian); 886 − 845 = 41.

body L12-L17: the dash after «II.» measures 10.0 pt; «Schiaparelli», «Martin», «Hipparchum» and «Ptolemaeus» are letter-spaced. «Th. M. Martin» (L12) is Thomas-Henri Martin, «Th. H. Martin» on p. 299, L25; the printed M is kept. 1° in 100 years is 36″ a year.

body L18-L25: «al–Farghānī», «al–Qazwīnī», «Al–Battānī» and «Menelai» are letter-spaced; «al–Farghānī», «al–Qazwīnī», «Al–Battānī» and «al–Battānī» (L22) have long dashes (5.5 pt each). The bar of the fraction of L22 prints only in short pieces. 11° 50′ in 782 years is 42600″ : 782 = 54″,4757 a year, as printed, or 54″ 28‴,5. With 54″ 28‴ = 3268‴, 1° = 216000‴ = 66 · 3268‴ + 312‴, so that 1° takes 66 312/3268 years, not the printed 66 318/3268; with 54″,4757 it takes 66 6/71 years. 3600″ : 66 = 54″ 32‴,7, the 54″ 33‴ of L25. The printed numbers are kept. Addenda, p. LXXVII («292–293»): Nallino does not know whence Gherardus of Sabbioneta took the statement (see his preface, p. XXXV–VI) that al-Battānī made the fixed stars move 1° in 60 years and 4 months; the same error stands in Baldi, p. 440 (extract p. 20).

body L26-L31: «aṣ–Ṣūfī» (L27, L29), «Filii», «Mūsà», «ibn Shākir», «al–Bīrūnī», «Ḥabash», «al–Kharaqī», «al–Khāzinī», «al–Ǵaghmīnī», «Barhebraeus» and «Chrysococcae» are letter-spaced; their long dashes and that of «al–Ma’mūn» measure 5.0 to 5.5 pt, and the dash after «(4).» 9.5 pt.
notes_left L3-L5: «Kugler» is letter-spaced; the dash of «103–104» is joined to the 3 and runs 4.5 pt beyond it, a long dash.
notes_left L6-L8: «Delambre» and «Tannery» are letter-spaced; «t. II.» has a full stop after the numeral, as printed. The 6 of «265-270» prints broken; its hyphen measures 2.4 pt.

notes_left L9-L12: «Bessel» is letter-spaced, and the ae of «praecessio» prints broken. The minus sign of the formula, at the end of L10, is a dash of 8.2 pt. For 880, t = 870 and 50″,21129 − 0″,0002442966 · 870 = 49″,99875, the 50″,0 of L12.
notes_right L1-L4: «Ibn Yūnus» and «Caussin» are letter-spaced. The full stop of «Paris.» (L4) did not print; a gap of its width (2.8 pt) stands before the comma.
notes_right L5-L9: the dash before «Iuxta» measures 7.3 pt; «Ibn Yūnus» (L6, L8), «Caussin», divided between L6 and L7, and «Ḥabash» are letter-spaced.

notes_right L10-L12: «Bullialdi» is letter-spaced; the initial I of «I. Bullialdi» prints without its serifs, like l, and a speck stands before it. Ismael Bullialdus' Astronomia philolaica appeared at Paris in 1645; «1545» is a misprint, kept as printed.
